title: El Niño and La Niña
description: The El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO): what it is, how it develops and how it affects weather worldwide.

questions.prompt: El Niño is an unusual warming of sea surface temperatures in which ocean region?
options: The central and eastern equatorial Pacific
questions.explanation: El Niño is defined by warm anomalies in the central and eastern tropical Pacific.

questions.prompt: What is the cool counterpart of El Niño called?
questions.explanation: La Niña brings cooler than average sea surface temperatures to the same region.

questions.prompt: What does ENSO stand for?
questions.explanation: ENSO links the ocean warming (El Niño) with a see-saw in air pressure (Southern Oscillation).

questions.prompt: During El Niño, the trade winds over the equatorial Pacific typically...
options: Turn to blow from north to south
questions.explanation: Weaker easterly trade winds let warm water spread east across the Pacific.

questions.prompt: Where does the name "El Niño" come from?
options: Fishers off Peru noticed warm water around Christmas and named it after the Christ child
A Spanish ship that first measured it
A storm that hit Mexico City
questions.explanation: "El Niño" means "the boy" or "the Christ child" in Spanish.

questions.prompt: The Southern Oscillation Index compares air pressure between which two places?
questions.explanation: Pressure at Tahiti (central Pacific) is compared with Darwin (northern Australia).

questions.prompt: El Niño typically brings drier than normal conditions to which region?
questions.explanation: Rainfall shifts east with the warm water, leaving the western Pacific drier.

questions.prompt: What happens to the upwelling of cold, nutrient-rich water off Peru during El Niño?
questions.explanation: Less upwelling means fewer nutrients, so fish such as anchovies decline.

questions.prompt: Which are common impacts of a strong El Niño?
options: Heavy rain and flooding in coastal Peru and Ecuador
A temporary rise in global average temperature
questions.explanation: El Niño usually suppresses Atlantic hurricanes through stronger wind shear.

questions.prompt: Which organisations monitor and forecast ENSO?
questions.explanation: National weather agencies and the WMO issue ENSO updates.

questions.prompt: Which measurements are used to monitor ENSO?
questions.explanation: ENSO is an ocean–atmosphere pattern; earthquakes are unrelated.

questions.prompt: An El Niño happens every single year.
questions.explanation: El Niño recurs irregularly, roughly every 2 to 7 years.

questions.prompt: A strong El Niño can temporarily raise the global average surface temperature.
questions.explanation: The Pacific releases heat to the atmosphere; record warm years often follow strong El Niños.

questions.prompt: La Niña brings cooler than average sea surface temperatures to the central and eastern equatorial Pacific.
questions.explanation: It is the cool phase of ENSO.

questions.prompt: El Niño and La Niña are the warm and cool phases of a climate pattern abbreviated as ___.
questions.explanation: ENSO = El Niño–Southern Oscillation.

questions.prompt: NOAA's main index for identifying El Niño and La Niña is the ___ Niño Index (ONI).
questions.explanation: The Oceanic Niño Index tracks sea surface temperature anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region.

questions.prompt: El Niño conditions require the ONI (3-month average temperature anomaly) to be at least how many °C above normal?
questions.explanation: An anomaly of +0.5 °C or more (and −0.5 °C or less for La Niña).

questions.prompt: Put the development of an El Niño event in order.
items: Trade winds over the equatorial Pacific weaken
Warm surface water spreads east from the western Pacific
Cold upwelling off South America decreases
Rainfall shifts east, leaving Indonesia and Australia drier
questions.explanation: Weaker winds let warm water move east, which suppresses upwelling and moves the rain with it.

questions.prompt: Put these strong El Niño events in chronological order.
questions.explanation: 1997–98 and 2015–16 are among the strongest El Niños on record.

questions.prompt: Match each term with its description.

pairs.right: Steady easterly winds near the equator
Cold, deep water rising to the surface

questions.explanation: These are the building blocks of the ENSO cycle.
